title: In characteristic p, injectivity of H_1(L_{K/k}) -> m/m^2 gives injectivity of Omega_{k/F_p} (x) K -> Omega_{A/F_p} (x) K
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic] and $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ a Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $K=A/\mathfrak m$; $k$, $A$, $K$ are $\mathbf F_p$-algebras. Let $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $H_1(L_{K/k})$ and $H_1(L_{K/A})$ be the first homologies of the naive cotangent complexes of the canonical presentations $k[K]\to K$ and $A[K]\to K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; the inclusion $k[K]\to A[K]$ is a morphism of presentations over the square $k\to A$, $\mathrm{id}_K$, and so induces a $K$-linear map $H_1(L_{K/k})\to H_1(L_{K/A})$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]; the canonical map $\gamma:H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is its composite with the isomorphism $H_1(L_{K/A})\cong\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] for the surjection $A\to K$. Let $\lambda:\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_AK$ be the $K$-linear map $\mathrm da\otimes x\mapsto\mathrm d(a\cdot1_A)\otimes x$. If $\gamma$ is injective, then $\lambda$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)' (lines 8763-8795): the Jacobi-Zariski sequences of F_p -> A -> K and F_p -> k -> K, with H_1(L_{K/A}) = m/m^2 and H_1(L_{K/F_p}) = 0 (Algebra 0322), show that the kernels of H_1(L_{K/k}) -> m/m^2 and of Omega_{k/F_p} (x) K -> Omega_{A/F_p} (x) K have the same dimension; the direction (3) => (4) is stated here, without the regularity of A, which the argument does not use (tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags: 07E5,more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular)

proof.text: The conormal equivalence in the statement is injective. Consequently, injectivity of γ implies injectivity of v = H1Cotangent.map k A K K: if v(h)=v(h′), applying that equivalence gives γ(h)=γ(h′).

Transfer characteristic p from k to K along the injective field algebra map. Apply the field prime-characteristic vanishing theorem; uniqueness of a ZMod p algebra structure identifies its algebra with the inherited residue-field algebra. Apply the first middle-exactness assertion to ZMod p → A → K. Its map v has subsingleton domain, so its range is zero, the kernel of ∂A is zero, and ∂A is injective.

Apply connecting-map naturality with R=ZMod p, S=k, B=A and I=maximalIdeal A. Its two identities imply ∂A composed with v equals c composed with ∂k by associativity. The target lambdaMap sends x tensor y to x tensor map(y): first use IsBaseChange.lift_eq at 1 tensor y, then K-linearity. The specified generator formula for c identifies it with lambdaMap; tensor extensionality and the surjective linear combination of universal differentials reduce this equality to x tensor D(s). Thus ∂A composed with v equals lambdaMap composed with ∂k.

The right square commutes: wA composed with lambdaMap equals wk. The universal property of differentials reduces the equality of the differential maps to D(s), where compatibility of k → A → K gives identical values. Tensor extensionality and the pure-tensor formula give the equality on all tensors.

For x with lambdaMap(x)=0 the right square gives wk(x)=0. The second middle-exactness assertion for ZMod p → k → K supplies h with ∂k(h)=x. The left square gives ∂A(v(h))=0. Injectivity of ∂A and then v implies h=0, hence x=0. The kernel of lambdaMap is zero, which is equivalent to injectivity.

All facts are cited existing reviewed nodes of unit sk-thm-p1; no new node was needed. Statement kept; the Noetherian hypothesis is kept as in the source though unused.
